threads.thread_goal: Align on scope and pick which vehicles join the initial pilot

messages.text:
Kicking off the Fleet Maintenance and Workshop Safety Standardization project for our yard. Goal is to reduce breakdowns and incidents by standardising daily checks and workshop routines, without adding extra people or blocking trucks during peak runs.
For the pilot in T10, we need to pick which vehicles and how many we start with, and align on how long we run it. My first thought is to focus on the highest-usage collection trucks so we see impact quickly.
Looking at the draft layout for the maintenance schedule board in A3 and the weekly deep-check idea in T2, it would help if the pilot set covers a mix of older and newer units.
Can you share which vehicles you think should be in the first batch, and any timing constraints from your shifts?

From late shift side, the rear-loader trucks 12, 14 and 18 give us the most trouble, especially with hydraulics and lights. They are also out almost every day.
If we include those three plus maybe one side-loader and one hook-lift, we would cover most of the issues we see.
For timing, if we avoid 5-9am and 4-7pm, we can do extra checks without holding up departures. I would suggest we start the pilot next Monday and run it for one full week so we can log issues properly for T10.

On early shift we see a lot of repeat defects on trucks 7 and 9, mainly tyres and warning lights. They are also high-usage.
If we already have three rear-loaders in the suggestion from 109283, maybe we pick just one of 7 or 9 so we do not overload the team.
I am ok with a one-week pilot, but I am not sure if we should start on Monday or mid-week so we can prepare the drivers. Maybe we need a short note for them first.

From the workshop side, trucks 12 and 18 are always in for leaks and small electrical fixes. If we put them in the pilot, we will need to be careful not to block bays.
I like the idea of mixing older and newer trucks. Maybe we also add one of the newer side-loaders, like 22, so we see if the new models need different checks.
About start date, I can adjust my tasks, but I would prefer if we do not start tomorrow. I still need to understand how the new daily checklist from T1 will look.

I agree with focusing on the trucks that are out every day. From my shift, truck 14 is the one that comes back with most notes from drivers.
For the pilot, could we keep it to five vehicles total so we can actually follow them properly on the board in A3 and not miss logs?
On timing, starting next Monday works for me. We can use the rest of this week to brief drivers and put up any visual aids we need.

Good point on driver prep. We should not surprise them with longer checks at the gate.
Proposal based on what you all shared:
- Vehicle types: mainly rear-loaders plus one side-loader and one hook-lift.
- Units: rear-loaders 12, 14, 18, side-loader 22, and one of 7 or 9.
That keeps us at five vehicles, as 156061 suggested, and matches the high-usage focus for T2 and T10.
On start date, I lean to next Monday so we can use the daily check-ins in this channel to remind everyone.

I am fine with that list. Between 7 and 9, I would pick 7. It has more mileage and more tyre issues.
If we confirm those five, I can start marking them on the draft schedule layout in A3 so we see them clearly during the pilot.

Ok, choosing truck 7 works for me. That gives us a good spread of issues to watch.
For the start date, next Monday is ok as long as we tell drivers by Friday. Maybe we can add a short note into the training brief draft in T8 so the message is consistent.

I am ok with those five trucks. I just worry a bit about bay space if more than two come in at once.
Maybe during the pilot we agree that deep checks from T2 on these trucks are done outside peak workshop times, like mid-morning and mid-afternoon, so we do not block urgent repairs.

Agree with the list and with starting Monday. For duration, one week sounds short but realistic for a first test. We can always extend later if needed.
During that week, we should log any delays or issues in the pilot summary in A8 so we have evidence when we adjust routines.

Sounds like we are converging.
To close this:
- Pilot vehicles: rear-loaders 12, 14, 18, 7; side-loader 22; hook-lift 1 (adding one hook-lift so we cover that type too, unless anyone objects).
- Pilot duration: one week.
- Pilot start: next Monday, with drivers briefed by Friday.
If no one raises a blocker by end of today, I will treat this as agreed and update the plan for T10 accordingly.

No blocker from my side. Adding hook-lift 1 is fine, it is not as busy as the others so we can manage the extra checks.
I will start marking these vehicles on the board layout in A3 and prepare a simple note for drivers based on what we will put into T8.
All good for early shift as well. I will remind drivers of these units during the morning check-in on Friday and Monday so they know we are testing new routines.
Ok for me too. I will keep an eye on bay usage that week and note any delays so we can add them into the pilot feedback in A8.
Agreed. I will help collect any comments from late shift drivers and add them to the T10 summary so we do not miss issues that only show up at night.
Thanks all. I will document the pilot scope and dates and share a short note here before Friday so everyone can point drivers to the same message.

threads.thread_goal: Draft and finalise the daily inspection checklist and weekly routine

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the daily vehicle inspection checklist for T1, based on what we already do plus some gaps we saw in the last month.
Structure in A1 draft:
- Exterior: body damage, mirrors, lights, indicators, licence plates.
- Tyres: pressure visual check, tread, obvious cuts.
- Fluids: oil level, coolant level, windscreen wash.
- Interior: horn, seatbelts, dashboard warning lights, cleanliness.
- Safety equipment: fire extinguisher, first aid kit, spill kit, reversing alarm.
Some of the deeper checks we currently do daily might be better as weekly in T2, like detailed brake inspection and full hydraulic hose check.
Can you review and say what is missing or too heavy for a daily routine?

Thanks for structuring it clearly.
From my side, the sections look right. For daily, I would keep anything that can be checked quickly without tools and that affects safety before leaving the yard.
I agree that detailed brake checks and full hydraulic inspections belong in the weekly deep-check in T2, not daily. For daily, maybe we just keep a simple leak and noise check when moving the vehicle.
One thing I would add to A1 is a quick check that the maintenance schedule status on the board in A3 matches the sticker in the cab, so we catch any mismatch early.

The structure makes sense to me. I just want to check one point: for fluids, are we expecting drivers to open the engine bay every day, or is that for us in the workshop?
On early shift, if drivers have to open everything, it might slow departures. Maybe we can say drivers do visual checks for leaks under the vehicle and dashboard warnings, and we do dipstick checks as part of a quick workshop pass twice a week?

I like that tyres and lights are clearly listed. Drivers often forget to mention small cuts on tyres.
For daily, I think we should keep a quick look at wheel nuts as well, at least visually, because we had that near-miss last year.
For weekly T2, we can add torque checks and more detailed tyre inspection, but that is more time-consuming.

From late shift, I would add a simple check that the cab is free of loose items that could roll under pedals. We see that a lot when trucks come back.
Also, for safety equipment, maybe we should specify that the fire extinguisher seal is intact and the gauge is in the green, not just that it is present.
I agree that full hydraulic hose checks should move to the weekly routine in T2. Daily, we can keep it to visible leaks and damaged hoses only.

Good question on fluids. My idea was:
- Drivers: check dashboard warnings and look for obvious leaks under the vehicle.
- Workshop: do dipstick and coolant level checks as part of a quick pass at least twice a week, and more detailed checks in the weekly deep-check in T2.
So in A1, we can split fluids into driver checks and workshop checks, and keep the daily part light for drivers.

I support that split. It respects the constraint of minimal downtime and keeps tasks aligned with who is best placed to do them.
For the weekly deep-check in T2, we should list clearly: full brake inspection, full hydraulic hose and fitting check, detailed tyre and wheel inspection including torque, and full fluid level check.
In A1, daily should stay as a one-page checklist that drivers and attendants can run through in under 10 minutes.

Ok, that makes sense. If we keep the daily checklist to one page and under 10 minutes, drivers will be more likely to follow it.
Could we add a small section at the bottom of A1 for notes, so they can write anything unusual that does not fit the boxes? That might help with T7 when we look for redundant steps later.

I have one doubt: should we include checking the reversing camera image daily, or is that part of the weekly routine?
It is quick to check, but sometimes the camera lens is dirty and drivers only notice on the road.

I would keep reversing camera and alarm in the daily checklist. It is a quick test and very important for safety in the yard.
For weekly, we can add cleaning of the camera housing and checking the wiring if there were any issues reported.

Agree with 156061. Reversing camera and alarm should stay in daily. The more we catch before moving the vehicle, the better.
So to summarise the split:
Daily (A1): quick visual checks of exterior, tyres, leaks, dashboard warnings, reversing aids, safety equipment, cab condition, and a quick match against the schedule board in A3.
Weekly (T2): detailed brakes, hydraulics, full fluid levels, detailed tyres and wheels including torque, deeper camera and wiring checks.
If everyone is ok with that, we can say the structure of the daily checklist is approved and these items move to weekly.

Works for me. I will update A1 to reflect the final structure and move the detailed items into the weekly routine draft for T2.
I will also add the notes section that 108987 suggested and keep it to one page.
I am ok with this split. Once you update A1, I can test it on two vehicles tomorrow and see if we stay under 10 minutes.
Fine for me too. When we map current steps for T7, we can compare the old and new daily checks and see if there is anything we can still remove.
Agreed. I will try the updated daily checklist on one of the pilot trucks during late shift and note any confusion from drivers so we can tweak wording if needed.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on hazardous substances handling rules and workshop standards

messages.text:
Starting a thread on hazardous substances and workshop standards.
I drafted some initial ideas for the handling and storage guide in A2 for T3 and for the cleaning and tool storage standard in A6 for T9.
Key points for chemicals and oils:
- All containers labelled with product name and hazard pictograms.
- Separate shelves for oils, cleaners, and fuels, with spill trays.
- PPE list by product type, based on safety data sheets.
- Simple spill response steps with where to find absorbent material.
For workshop organisation:
- Marked zones for tools, waste, and chemicals.
- End-of-shift checklist for sweeping, putting tools back, and emptying waste bins.
Please comment on what is practical for your shift and what we might be missing.

For early shift, the main issue I see is open containers of degreaser and oil left on benches.
Could we add a rule in A2 that all liquids must be stored with lids on when not in use, and that we do not use unlabelled bottles at all?
On cleaning, the end-of-shift checklist in A6 sounds good, but we need to keep it short so people actually do it. Maybe three or four clear steps only.

I agree on the labels. Sometimes we pour cleaner into old drink bottles, which is not safe.
Maybe we should say in T3 that only approved containers from the store can be used, and if a label is damaged, we replace it before using the product.
For tool zones in T9, could we mark the floor with colours so it is obvious where tools and waste go? That might help new staff.

On late shift we often handle used oil and coolant when draining vehicles.
I suggest A2 includes:
- Separate labelled drums for used oil and used coolant.
- Clear rule that we never mix different wastes in the same drum.
- Simple instruction on what to do if a drum is nearly full, so we do not overfill.
For A6, I like the idea of an end-of-shift checklist. Maybe we can also add a quick check that spill kits are complete and in place.

One thing I see a lot is rags soaked in solvent left on benches.
Could we define in T9 that there is a metal bin with lid just for oily and solvent rags, and that it is emptied into the correct waste container at least once per shift?
Also, for PPE in A2, maybe we can have a simple table on the wall: for each product, which gloves, goggles, and mask to use. That would make it easier to follow.

These are all good additions.
On the rules side, I propose we lock in the following for A2:
- Only labelled, approved containers from the store, no drink bottles.
- Lids on when not in use.
- Separate storage and waste drums for each type of oil and coolant, clearly labelled.
- PPE table on the wall by product.
- Simple spill response: stop, contain, clean, report, with location of spill kits.
If we agree, we can say the handling and storage rules are approved and send A2 to the health and safety officer for sign-off as required in T3.

I am ok with those rules. They match what we should already be doing, just clearer.
For workshop standards in A6 and T9, I suggest the end-of-shift checklist includes:
- Tools back in marked places.
- Floors swept in work areas.
- Waste bins and oily rag bin checked and emptied if needed.
- Chemicals shelves checked for open containers and spills wiped.

That list looks manageable. I just want to be sure it does not take too long at the end of shift.
Maybe we can say the end-of-shift cleaning should take about 10 minutes, and if there is a big spill or job still open, we note it in the handover template in A5 instead of trying to finish everything.

I agree with the four steps. To make T9 clear, we can define zones like this:
- Blue zone: tools and equipment.
- Yellow zone: waste and oily rag bins.
- Red zone: chemicals and oils.
We can mark these on the floor and on shelves so new staff can see quickly where things belong.

I like the idea of linking big clean-ups to the handover notes in A5. That way the next shift knows there is still work to do and why the area is not perfect.
For A6, maybe we can add a small tick-box form near the exit so the last person out can quickly tick off the four steps.

So for workshop standards, we have:
- Clearly marked zones for tools, waste, and chemicals as part of T9.
- End-of-shift checklist with four steps, taking about 10 minutes.
- Oily rag bin with lid, emptied at least once per shift.
- Quick tick-box form at the exit, and use of A5 handover notes if something big is left open.
If everyone is comfortable with that, we can say the end-of-shift cleaning and tool storage standards are agreed and finalise A6 and T9.
Agreed from my side. Once A2 and A6 are updated, I can walk through them with the early shift team and check if anything is unclear.
Ok for me too. I will pay attention to how long the end-of-shift steps actually take this week and let you know if we need to adjust.
All good. I can help mark the zones on the floor and set up the oily rag bin once we have the final A6 printed.
Agreed. I will check that spill kits and PPE tables from A2 are in place during late shift and note any missing items.

threads.thread_goal: Define how incidents, near-misses and 'do not use' vehicles are flagged

messages.text:
Yesterday we had a small incident: a driver almost moved truck 14 while a hose was still connected. He stopped in time, so no damage, but it was close.
I was not sure how to log this properly. For T5 we have the idea of an incident and near-miss log in A4, but I do not know exactly which fields we want or how we flag the vehicle as not safe to leave the yard.
Can we agree what information we record in A4 and how we mark a 'do not use' vehicle for T11?

Thanks for raising it, that is exactly the kind of near-miss we want to capture.
For A4, I suggest we keep the fields simple:
- Date and time.
- Vehicle ID.
- Location (yard, workshop bay, on route).
- Type (incident or near-miss).
- Short description of what happened.
- Immediate action taken.
- Follow-up action needed and by when.
For 'do not use' in T11, we need both a physical tag on the vehicle and a note on the schedule board in A3 so no one misses it.

For the log, could we also have a field for who reported it? Sometimes we hear about things second-hand and it is hard to follow up.
On 'do not use', I have seen other yards use red tags on the steering wheel. Maybe we can do something similar and also put a red magnet on the board in A3.

I like the idea of red tags. For T11, we should also define clear criteria for when we use them, so we do not overuse or underuse.
Maybe:
- Any brake or steering issue.
- Any major fluid leak.
- Any safety equipment failure that affects safe operation, like no reversing alarm or serious lighting fault.
- Any structural damage that could affect stability.
If one of these is found during the daily check in A1, we tag the vehicle and log it in A4.

For the near-miss you mentioned, I would log it as 'near-miss, hose still connected when driver tried to move'.
In A4, maybe we can add a simple checkbox for 'discussed in weekly review' so we know if we already talked about it in the T12 meeting.
On 'do not use', I agree with red steering wheel tags plus a mark on the board. We just need to be clear who is allowed to remove the tag once the issue is fixed.

The criteria you listed make sense. I just wonder about smaller issues like a cracked mirror. That is not as serious as brakes, but still important.
Should we have a separate 'use with caution' note for those, or just log them in A4 and fix as soon as possible without tagging the vehicle?

Good distinction.
I would keep 'do not use' tags in T11 for issues that make the vehicle unsafe to operate at all, like the list 109283 shared.
For smaller but important issues like cracked mirrors or minor leaks, we log them in A4 and mark them as 'defect only' without tagging the vehicle, but we still set a due date for repair.
That way the log in A4 covers both incidents and defects, but the red tag is reserved for critical cases.

Who will be allowed to put and remove the red tags? I think it should not be everyone, or we might get confusion.
Maybe only attendants and the fleet supervisor can put a 'do not use' tag, and only they can remove it after checking the repair.

I agree. We can write in T11 that attendants and the fleet supervisor are responsible for tagging and untagging.
Also, when we remove a tag, we should update A4 with the date and note that the vehicle is cleared, and change the status on the board in A3 from red back to normal.

For the log fields in A4, I like what 203126 proposed. I would just add 'shift' so we know if it happened on early or late.
So final list would be: date, time, shift, vehicle, location, type, description, immediate action, follow-up action and due date, reporter, discussed in weekly review, and cleared date if it was a 'do not use' case.

That covers what we need without making it too heavy.
To close this:
- A4 will have the fields you listed: date, time, shift, vehicle, location, type, description, immediate action, follow-up and due date, reporter, discussed in weekly review, and cleared date.
- 'Do not use' in T11 will apply to critical safety issues only, with red steering wheel tags and red magnets on A3.
- Only attendants and the fleet supervisor can apply and remove tags, and they must update A4 and the board when they do.
If everyone agrees, we can say the log process and visual method are confirmed.
Agreed. I will log yesterday's near-miss in A4 using the new fields and tag truck 14 as needed if we find any damage during checks.
Ok for me. I will prepare a small batch of red tags and magnets so we can start using the process this week.
All good. I will test the log with a couple of sample incidents to make sure A4 is easy to fill and we are not missing anything before we roll it out fully.
Agreed as well. During the first weekly review in T12, we can check if the new log and tags are working as expected.

threads.thread_goal: Plan training, shift handovers and weekly review cadence

messages.text:
We also need to align on how we train people on the new routines, how we do shift handovers, and how we run weekly reviews.
For T6 and A5, I drafted a simple handover template with:
- Open jobs by vehicle, with priority.
- Parts on order.
- Safety issues to highlight.
- Notes for the next shift.
For T8 and A7, the training brief covers the daily checklist, weekly deep-check, schedule board, incident log, and 'do not use' tags.
For T12, we need a weekly review slot and who should attend.
Proposal:
- Handover notes filled at the end of each shift for any open items.
- Short training for drivers and attendants using A7 before the pilot starts.
- Weekly review every Tuesday at 10:00 with at least one person from each shift.
Please share if this works for your shifts and what we should adjust.

For early shift, end-of-shift handover in A5 is fine, but sometimes we are rushed at the end.
Could we say that we only need to fill A5 when there are open jobs or safety issues, not every single day with 'nothing to report'?
On training, a short session using A7 before the pilot sounds good. Maybe 20 minutes at the start of shift.

I like having a clear place to write open jobs and parts on order. Right now we sometimes just tell each other verbally and things get lost.
For T6, could we add a field in A5 for 'blocked vehicles' so we can quickly see which ones are tagged 'do not use'?
About the weekly review at 10:00, I might not always be free if we have urgent repairs, but I can try to join when possible.

For late shift, end-of-shift handover is very useful because the next team is usually early shift.
I support filling A5 whenever there are open jobs, safety issues, or 'do not use' tags, and we can skip it if everything is clear.
On the weekly review in T12, Tuesday at 10:00 works for me. I can represent late shift there and bring any points from the team.

For training, I think we should keep A7 very simple and visual, maybe with one example of a good daily checklist and one of a good incident log entry.
On handovers, could we also mention in A5 if there were any near-misses that day, so the next shift is aware even before it appears in A4?

Good point on not overloading people.
For A5 and T6, we can define that the handover template must be filled whenever there are:
- Open jobs that will continue into the next shift.
- Safety issues or 'do not use' tags.
- Significant incidents or near-misses.
If there is truly nothing to report, we can skip filling it that day.
That works for me. I will start using A5 like that from tomorrow and see how it goes.
Ok, clear. I will remember to add blocked vehicles and near-misses into A5 when they happen.

On the weekly review in T12, Tuesday at 10:00 is fine. I suggest we keep the agenda simple:
- Review the schedule board A3 for overdue services.
- Review A4 for incidents and near-misses.
- Agree two or three improvement actions and who owns them.
That should keep the meeting under 30 minutes.

I like that agenda. For attendance, I think we need at least one attendant from each shift and the fleet supervisor or their delegate.
If someone cannot join, they can leave notes in A5 or in this channel before the meeting.

Agreed on the agenda and attendance.
So for T12 we will set a recurring weekly review on Tuesdays at 10:00, with at least one person from early and late shifts plus the fleet supervisor or delegate.
We will use A3 and A4 as the main inputs and capture at least two improvement actions each time.
If there are no objections, we can treat this as confirmed.
No objection from me. I will block that time in my calendar and make sure someone from early shift is always there.

On the training brief in A7, I sometimes struggle with long documents.
Could we keep it to two pages with simple language and maybe some pictures of the checklist A1, the board A3, and the incident log A4? That would help new staff a lot.

The definition for T8 already says under two pages, so that fits well.
I can help by taking photos of the board and a filled-in checklist so we can add them to A7.

For the actual training sessions, maybe we can run two short briefings per shift: one focused on drivers and one on attendants.
Drivers: focus on A1, 'do not use' tags, and how to report incidents in A4.
Attendants: focus on A1, T2 weekly checks, A3 board, A5 handover, and A6 cleaning standard.
We can use A7 as the base for both.

That split makes sense and keeps each session focused.
To summarise this thread:
- A5 handover template will be filled at the end of any shift with open jobs, safety issues, 'do not use' tags, or significant incidents or near-misses.
- Weekly review for T12 will be every Tuesday at 10:00 with at least one person from each shift and the fleet supervisor or delegate, using A3 and A4.
- Training brief A7 will be under two pages, simple language, with visuals, and we will run short sessions for drivers and attendants before the pilot.
With that, I think we can say the handover template usage and weekly review slot are approved.
Agreed. I will start using the new handover template and help with the first driver briefing on early shift.
All good from late shift. I will support with photos and help run the attendant training using A7.
Ok for me too. Once A7 is final, I will keep a printed copy in the workshop so new starters can read it on their first day.
Agreed. I will join the Tuesday reviews whenever possible and bring feedback from late shift on how the routines are working.
